newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - T-BONDS FAIL TO RETEST RECENT HIGHS.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-BONDS FAIL TO RETEST RECENT HIGHS.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures failed again Thursday to regain bullish momentum, suggesting to some analysts that the market may have put in a long-term top at the 116-31 high reached last week.

Gerry DeMers, technical analyst with Fuji Securities Inc, noted hourly stochastics turned down at midmorning, moving in line with the daily and weekly indicators to suggest the trend has changed to lower.
He said he would recommend selling any bounces, though he thought the market would have a hard time rebounding from current losses.
Bond futures were down about 1/2 point late in the day at 114-09/32.
September futures would be a sell on a bounce back to 115-11/32, a level representing the 38.2 percent retracement back from the early-week lows to the 116-31 high, said DeMers.
"I'm of the opinion that that was the high," he said. "Your risk reversal is you've got a good multi-point move down."

Dave Toth, vice president with Optima Institutional Services, said he also suspected 116-31 was a major top for bond futures based on a combination of factors, including overly bullish sentiment on the 10-point-plus rise from April, momentum indicators and Elliott Wave analysis.
"The combination of the extreme optimism and bearish divergence in momentum increase the possibility that the 116-31 high put in a fifth wave," Toth said.
First, however, the analyst said he looked for futures to regain the 115-20/32 level or higher over the next week.
"That will be an exquisite risk reversal situation from which to establish a long-term bearish policy," Toth said.
